resource.name: OKR Critique
resource.description: Paste draft OKRs. Returns four-test critique per KR (outcome-vs-activity, measurable, single-team-fit, too-many), stance-specific synthesis, and a rewritten set.

tools.name: okr_parse
tools.description: Deterministic. Extracts objectives and key results from free-form pasted text. Returns structured form for downstream critique.

tools.name: okr_critique
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Runs four-test critique per KR (outcome-vs-activity, measurable, single-team-fit, too-many), produces per-KR diagnosis + rewrite + anchor.

rewrite.description: Optional. Omitted when no rewrite is needed.

tools.name: okr_org_coherence
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Org-level cross-team coherence check across multiple objectives. Surfaces internal contradictions and KR-ownership ambiguity.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Available in both web and MCP versions, but only triggered when level == 'org'.

tools.name: okr_mortality
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Ingests actual quarterly outcomes after the fact. Surfaces which OKRs were rewritten mid-quarter vs achieved as-stated. Pattern: high mid-quarter rewrites = theatre. Stores quarterly OKRs and outcomes locally across runs.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Web version does not expose this. Mortality analysis requires persisted prior OKRs + outcomes in the .mcpb bundle's data dir; host's confirmation UI handles the consent surface.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #24 OKR Critique. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Validated against MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026 release + current draft) on 2026-05-18.

dev.workingfromlenny.app.name: OKR Critique
dev.workingfromlenny.app.type: paste + LLM critique with stance picker

dev.workingfromlenny.open_questions: Org-level coherence: what's the right max-objectives input cap? More than 8 starts to read as 'we're doing too many things' rather than a coherence problem.
okr_mortality: should the tool prompt the user for outcomes per KR, or pull from connected analytics? Latter is a hard dependency.
Should the four-test verdicts be configurable (some teams reject 'too-many' as a test) or locked? Locked is simpler; configurable is closer to how teams actually argue about OKRs.
dev.workingfromlenny.proposed_answers: Cap at 8 objectives for the okr_org_coherence tool. The observation in the question is correct: an input of 12 objectives calls for 'pick the five that matter' before coherence analysis. Set maxItems: 8 in the inputSchema (now applied above), and if the input exceeds 8, the schema-level validation rejects it before the coherence pass runs.

User-entered outcomes for Phase 2, structured as free-text per KR. The analytics integration is a hard dependency that makes Phase 2 deployment conditional on external tooling not under the owner's control. Free-text entry ('KR: Ship checkout redesign by Q1 — what actually happened?') is sufficient for the mortality pattern and aligns with how retrospectives actually run. Flag the analytics pull as a Phase 3 upgrade.

Lock the four tests for Phase 2. They are corpus-anchored and form a coherent framework. Use the existing stance parameter (orthodox / skeptical / hybrid) to adjust how aggressively the tests are applied: teams that resist the 'too-many' test tend to be operating in the skeptical stance already. Configurable tests add surface area and break the teachable-standard-set framing. Revisit in Phase 3.
_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.outputSchema_refact: Removed `type: ['string', 'null']` on `rewrite` field; changed to plain optional string. Absent fields are unambiguous; explicit nulls add a deserialization edge case.

notes: ui:// scheme is valid; no rigid format is enforced — server-defined slugs after the scheme are acceptable.

No requires-consent / data-retention / fs-write capability exists in either ext-apps appCapabilities or .mcpb manifest. Consent is host-discretion; readOnlyHint: false on stateful tools is the only normative hook.
Underscore-prefixed fields at non-_meta paths have undefined host behavior; project metadata lives under _meta with reverse-DNS keys.
